t.1.55.2: I shall set forth in full the doctrine of this wise great seer Vyāsa, of boundless splendor, who is renowned throughout all the worlds.
t.1.55.1: Having first bowed to my guru with mind, intellect and full concentration, and having honored all the twice-born as well as the other learned people,
t.1.55.4: Listen, O king, to how the split between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas came about over the kingdom, arising from the dice game, and likewise how the forest exile came to pass.
t.1.55.3: You, O king, are a worthy vessel for hearing, and having received this tale of the Bhāratas, the stirring of my guru seems joyfully to urge me on to tell it.
t.1.55.5: And how the war came about that brought destruction upon the earth, that I shall fully relate to you, since you ask, O bull of the Bharatas.
t.1.55.6: When their father had died, those heroes came from the forest to their own home, and before long they became learned in the Veda and in the science of the bow.
t.1.55.8: Then cruel Duryodhana and Karṇa, together with Saubala, devised against them various means of restraint and banishment.
t.1.55.7: Seeing the Pāṇḍavas thus endowed with beauty, valor and vigor, esteemed by the townspeople and bearing prosperity and fame, the Kurus could not endure it.
t.1.55.9: Then the wicked son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra gave poison to Bhīma, but the hero Vṛkodara digested it along with his food.
t.1.55.11: When the son of Kuntī awoke, then, O great king, Bhīmasena cut through his bonds and rose up, freed from his pain.
t.1.55.10: Then, at Pramāṇakoṭi, he bound Vṛkodara as he lay fast asleep, and having thrown Bhīma into the waters of the Gaṅgā, he returned to the city.
t.1.55.12: And while he slept, he had him bitten by venomous black snakes on every part of his body, yet the slayer of foes did not die.
t.1.55.13: But in each and every one of those injuries done to them, the great-minded Vidura was ever watchful, both to free them and to ward off the harm.
t.1.55.14: Just as Śakra, abiding in heaven, brings happiness to the world of living beings, so too Vidura always brings happiness to the Pāṇḍavas.
t.1.55.15: But when, by various means, both secret and open, he was unable to kill them, for they were protected by fate for the sake of a purpose yet to come,
t.1.55.17: There he made the Pāṇḍavas of boundless might dwell, and then, while they were trusting and unsuspecting, he had them burned with fire.
t.1.55.16: Then, having consulted with his counselors, Vṛṣa, Duḥśāsana and the others, and having obtained Dhṛtarāṣṭra's permission, he ordered a house of lac to be built.
t.1.55.19: Then, in a great and dreadful forest, the enraged Bhīmasena, of terrible prowess, slew on the earth a rākṣasa named Hiḍimba.
t.1.55.18: Then, at Vidura's word alone, a digger was engaged, who freed them by a skilful device; once released, they fled out of fear.
t.1.55.21: There, having slain the mighty Baka for the sake of a brāhmaṇa, they then went, accompanied by brāhmaṇas, to the city of the Pāñcālas.
t.1.55.20: Then those heroes, scorchers of foes, having made their resolve, took on the guise of brahmins and went with their mother to Ekacakrā.
t.1.55.22: Having won Draupadī there and having dwelt there a full year, those tamers of their foes, now known to all, returned to Hāstinapura.
t.1.55.24: Therefore, with your anger gone, go and dwell in Khāṇḍavaprastha, which is furnished with settled country and has well-laid-out highways.
t.1.55.23: They were told by King Dhṛtarāṣṭra and by Śāṃtanava: “So that there may be no strife between you and your brothers, dear son, we have resolved that you should dwell in Khāṇḍavaprastha.”
t.1.55.25: At the word of those two, they went to the city of Khāṇḍavaprastha together with all their friends, taking with them treasures of every kind.
t.1.55.26: There they dwelt, O king, for many years, bringing other kings under their sway by the might of their weapons.
t.1.55.27: Thus they, with dharma foremost, devoted to their vows of truth, vigilant and ever active, forbearing, then went on scorching their foes.
t.1.55.28: Bhīmasena of great strength conquered the eastern quarter, the heroic Arjuna the northern, and Nakula likewise the western.
t.1.55.29: Sahadeva, slayer of enemy heroes, conquered the southern region. In this way they all brought this entire earth under their control.
t.1.55.30: With the five Pāṇḍavas of true valour, resembling suns, and with the shining sun itself, the earth appeared as though it had six suns.
t.1.55.31: Then, on a certain occasion, Yudhiṣṭhira, the king of dharma, sent his brother Dhanaṃjaya away to the forest.
t.1.55.32: He dwelt in the forest for a full year and one month. Then, at one time, he went to Hṛṣīkeśa in Dvāravatī.
t.1.55.33: There Bībhatsu won as his wife the lotus-eyed Subhadrā of gracious speech, the younger sister of Vāsudeva.
t.1.55.34: Like Śacī united with great Indra, like Śrī joined with Kṛṣṇa, so Subhadrā, delighted, was joined with Arjuna the Pāṇḍava.
t.1.55.35: And Kaunteya Bībhatsu, together with Vāsudeva, satisfied the oblation-bearer Agni in the Khāṇḍava forest, O best of kings.
t.1.55.36: For with Keśava at his side it was no excessive burden for Pārtha, whose ally was resolve, just as it is none for Viṣṇu in the slaying of his foes.
t.1.55.37: And Agni also gave to Pārtha the supreme bow Gāṇḍīva, two quivers with inexhaustible arrows, and a chariot bearing the monkey emblem.
t.1.55.38: There Bībhatsu set free Maya, the great Asura, and he built a divine assembly hall, filled with every kind of jewel.
t.1.55.40: He sent them away to the forest for seven years and five, and likewise for a thirteenth year to be spent unrecognized in the kingdom.
t.1.55.39: Foolish and exceedingly evil-minded Duryodhana conceived a greed for it; and then, having cheated Yudhiṣṭhira with the dice through Saubala,
t.1.55.41: Then, in the fourteenth year, though they asked for their own wealth, they did not obtain it, great king; then war broke out.
t.1.55.43: Thus, O best of victors, is this ancient account of those men of tireless deeds: their division, the loss of their kingdom, and their victory.
t.1.55.42: Then the Pāṇḍavas, having destroyed everything and slain King Duryodhana, took possession of the kingdom, which had for the most part been laid waste.
